newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia urged to develop coal seam methane.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia urged to develop coal seam methane.

text.p: Economic incentives similar to those in the United States are needed to boost development of Australia's coal seam methane industry, a leading gas industry developer said on Friday.

Cooperation between the mining and petroleum industries in Australia would also be vital to the industry's success, Conoco Australia Pty Ltd vice-president Eric Miller told the Australian Mining Conference on the Gold Coast.
"Economic incentives provided in the United States by the Section 29 tax credit are non-existent in Australia," he said.
"Australia currently provides very little in the way of economic incentive that will stimulate growth of the coal seam methane industry," Miller said.
The next two years were likely to be a watershed in the development of Australia's, and in particular Queensland's, coal seam methane industry, he said.
"If Bowen Basin coal seam methane can be developed into a commercial resource, Queensland's industrial base will expand significantly," Miller said.
Conoco, a division of Dupont Co, was confident that technical problems associated with coal seam methane production would be overcome, he said.

Miller, who is also Conoco Australia's general manager, business development, said a prime factor in successful development of the U.S. coal seam methane industry was co-operation between the petroleum and mining industries.
"It was the two industries working together which helped expedite growth in technical acheivement," he said.
"This co-operation between industries is currently lacking in Australia," he said.
By adopting U.S.-developed technologies, Australia may begin higher up the learning curve, Miller said.
"However significant time and capital investment will still be required," he said.
One of the critical elements was infrastructure with Australia currently lacking any interstate gas network to provide an expanding market for methane gas, Miller said.
"Until such a system is in place, development of coal seam methane will be restricted to providing local gas requirements or satisfying local industrial expansion," he said.

Miller said Conoco Australia had already invested more than A$70 million in coal seam methane exploration and by the end of 1996 would have spent A$120 million to develop coal seam methane into a commercial resource.
Conoco currently had more than 33 wells under test in the Bowen Basin with spot market gas sales expected to begin this month, he said.
"Benefits derived from developing (Australia's) abundant coal seam methane resources will be significant," Miller said.
